headline: 作家 Eggers：AI 寫作代勞是人類末路
context: 美國作家 Dave Eggers 新書出版，他在採訪中直言：「一旦讓機器替你思考、替你寫作，你就作為一個物種完蛋了。」他曾與 OpenAI 執行長 Sam Altman 公開辯論 AI 對創作的影響，其新小說背景設定在藝術世界。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: As his new novel is published, the US author talks about nurturing the next generation of creatives, debating Sam Altman – and why he writes on a boat in San Francisco Bay At Dave Eggers’s suggestion, we’re starting the interview by life drawing together. The novelist dropped out of art school but has been drawing for decades, and his new book is set in the art world. Prudence, our model, stands before us with her palms open, nude but for a pair of black knee-high socks. This, unsurprisingly, is an interview first for me. Eggers shows me how to hold my pencil at arm’s length and use my thumb to measure Prudence’s proportions. Since the pandemic, he’s been organising regular life‑drawing sessions in the book-lined offices of McSweeney’s, the publishing house and literary journal he founded in San Francisco in 1998. He loves the element of chance in figure drawing – you never know which sketch will work out – and believes it helps cultivate empathy. How so, asks Prudence, helpfully interviewing him for me, because I’ve been thrown off my game. “I feel like in three hours of drawing a human, you learn so much about them and there is so much affection that comes from carefully trying to get them right,” he says. sources.title: Dave Eggers: ‘Once you have a machine think and write for you, you’re cooked as a species’

thread_text:
美國作家 Dave Eggers 新書出版。採訪中，他說了一句直接的話：「一旦你讓機器替你思考、替你寫作，你就作為一個物種完蛋了。」

Eggers 是舊金山文學出版社兼文學誌《McSweeney's》的創辦人，1998 年創立，他在一艘停在舊金山灣上的船上寫作，也曾與 OpenAI 執行長 Sam Altman 就 AI 對創作的影響公開辯論。他的新小說場景設定在藝術世界。

—— 本則來自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 6 月 27 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

他的新小說場景設定在藝術世界，本人也持續在《McSweeney's》辦公室舉辦素描課，他認為仔細描繪一個人能培養對人的同理心。
